essence: Give every new habit a time, a place and an anchor.
modern_lens: Chapter 5 shows that vague intentions fail and specific plans succeed. 'I will exercise more' loses to 'I will walk for twenty minutes at 7am on the canal path'. At work, tying a new habit to a standing meeting, the commute or the first coffee turns a good intention into a reliable routine.

ideas.name: Implementation Intentions
ideas.text: A plan that names the behaviour, the time and the place (I will do X at time Y in place Z) is far more likely to happen than a general intention. Specific plans remove the daily decision about when and where.
ideas.try: Write one sentence: I will [habit] at [time] in [place]. Put it in your calendar.

ideas.name: Clarity Beats Motivation
ideas.text: Many people think they lack motivation when they actually lack clarity. When it is not obvious when and where to act, the moment slips past. A clear plan lets you act even on a low-energy day.
ideas.try: Take one goal you keep postponing and decide exactly when and where the next step happens.

ideas.name: Habit Stacking
ideas.text: Link a new habit to one you already do every day: after my current habit, I will do the new habit. The existing routine becomes the cue. Small stacks can chain into a dependable morning or end-of-day sequence.
ideas.try: Write one stack: After I [daily habit], I will [new two-minute habit].

ideas.name: Choose the Right Anchor
ideas.text: A stack works only if the anchor happens at the right time, in the right place and as often as the new habit should. 'After I close my laptop for the day' is a strong anchor for a shutdown review; 'when I feel stressed' is too vague.
ideas.try: List ten things you do every day without fail and pick the best anchor for your new habit.

ideas.name: One Change Leads to Another
ideas.text: A new purchase or behaviour tends to pull related ones along with it, like a new sofa that suddenly makes the old rug look shabby. Use this chain reaction on purpose by designing each habit to trigger the next useful step.
ideas.try: Choose a habit you already do well and add one small step that naturally follows it.
